title: Explicit continuous unit-pivot Schur elimination
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative topological ring, let $T$ be a topological space, let $m,n\geq1$, and let $K:T\to\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m}(A)$ [def-weil-matrix] have entrywise continuous entries. Suppose $a(t)=K_{11}(t)$ is a unit for every $t$ and $t\mapsto a(t)^{-1}$ is continuous. Define $L_0(t)$ to be diagonal with $a(t)^{-1}$ in the $(1,1)$ position and $1$ elsewhere, define $R_0(t)$ to be the identity with $(1,j)$ entry $-a(t)^{-1}K_{1j}(t)$ for $j>1$, and define $L_1(t)$ to be the identity with $(i,1)$ entry $-a(t)^{-1}K_{i1}(t)$ for $i>1$. Put $L(t)=L_0(t)L_1(t)$ and $H_{ij}(t)=K_{ij}(t)-a(t)^{-1}K_{i1}(t)K_{1j}(t)$ for $i,j$ in the reduced index sets. Then $L$ and $R_0$ are entrywise continuous maps to $\operatorname{GL}_n(A)$ and $\operatorname{GL}_m(A)$ with entrywise continuous inverses, $H$ has continuous entries, and $L(t)K(t)R_0(t)=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&H(t)\end{pmatrix}$ for every $t$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.12(2), finite E case, pp. 18–19: continuous integral division and elementary pivot elimination; the displayed auxiliary statement is written out here because HRS uses it as a standard calculation.
